title: Garment workers block highway in Dhaka demanding wage hike and arrears

tea.why: Garment workers protested due to soaring prices of daily essentials and unpaid arrears.
tea.want: They demanded higher wages, lower prices for essential commodities, payment of arrears, and other benefits.
tea.changed: Oct 16: Police dispersed protesters from the Azampur road after a blockade lasting nearly four hours.

summary: Garment workers from several factories staged demonstrations blocking sections of the Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway in Dhaka's Uttara area across multiple days, including Rajlokkhi and Azampur. The protesters chanted slogans and halted traffic to demand wage increases, the lowering of essential commodity prices, and the payment of outstanding wages and benefits. According to police, the demonstrations caused severe traffic congestion. Authorities eventually intervened and dispersed the workers from the roadway.
demands: Lower the prices of essential commodities
response: According to police officials, officers intervened and dispersed the garment workers from the roadway after an extended period of traffic disruption, as confirmed by Uttara East Police Station officer-in-charge Md Morshed Alam and Uttara West Police Station officer-in-charge Khalid Mansur.

crowd.text: More than 1,000 workers from several garment factories took to the streets

updates.text: Garment workers staged demonstrations for consecutive days over wage increases and outstanding payments.
Protests continued along key points of the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway for a third consecutive day.
Workers blocked the highway in Uttara's Rajlokkhi and Azampur areas, causing severe traffic jams.
Police dispersed the demonstrators from the Azampur road, ending the morning blockade.
